project.domain: public-sector data quality, drift and decision monitoring

thesis: Core signals are computed deterministically from explicit data-quality and statistical contracts; an LLM may explain evidence later but does not own calculation or consequential authority.

evidence.claim: Compute first, explain second, human decides; no LLM owns the calculation or decision boundary.
The current core has no autonomous agent or tool execution path.
The portfolio proof uses deterministic synthetic administrative data and does not expose a multi-tenant production workload.
Signals trigger review; no individual benefit, enforcement or discrimination decision is automated.
Signal evidence exposes baseline/recent windows, sample sizes, effect sizes, confidence intervals and explicit thresholds.
No real citizen data is used in the work sample.
There is no autonomous model/tool loop in the current product path.
Deterministic data generation, data quality, PSI, statistical signals, decision boundaries and presentation values are regression-tested.
Every surfaced signal exposes the evidence and interpretation boundary a human should inspect.
The current work sample does not claim complete production dependency or source-system provenance assurance.
Current tests validate injected drift and negative decision boundaries, but there is no dedicated malicious data-poisoning/security gauntlet yet.
SignalLab implements monitoring logic for data quality/drift, while real production ingestion, SLOs and incident response remain out of scope.

adversarial.taxonomy: No dedicated malicious data-poisoning/security gauntlet published yet

residualRisks: Current drift/data-quality tests are correctness and monitoring evidence, not a malicious data-poisoning red-team suite.
Source spoofing, schema poisoning, metric manipulation and adversarial missingness need dedicated attack fixtures.
Real multi-source ingestion, production ETL contracts and operational security monitoring remain out of scope.
No real citizen data or actual DRV decision rules are used or claimed.
